text_blocks.snippet: Common and emerging scams actively reported across Central Illinois include:
Top Active Scams in Central Illinois

list.snippet: AI-Powered Voice & Imposter Calls: Scammers use artificial intelligence voice-cloning technology and spoofed numbers to mimic family members or law enforcement/federal prosecutors (such as the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of Illinois), demanding immediate payment or threats of arrest .
Jury Duty Scams: Fraudsters pose as local sheriff's deputies (e.g., in Macon County and Peoria County), claiming the victim missed jury duty and must pay a fine or resolve a citation immediately.

Extortion & Bitcoin Email Scams: Scammers email targets their real name, phone number, and street view image of their house, falsely claiming to have explicit photos and demanding a Bitcoin payment to delete them.

Secretary of State / DMV / Toll Text Scams: Fraudulent text messages falsely claim recipients owe money for traffic violations, tolls, or license/registration issues, or are due a refund. (The Illinois Secretary of State does not send texts regarding traffic or license suspensions) .
Romance Scams: Scammers build long-term online emotional connections with victims before manipulating them into sending thousands of dollars.
Driveway Paving & Home Improvement Scams: Itinerant contractors show up offering quick-fix or leftover-material deals for paving and repairs, leaving subpar or unfinished work.

Hang up and verify independently: If a caller claims to be from a government agency, court, or sheriff's office, hang up and call the official published number directly—never use the number provided by the caller.
Establish a family codeword: Agree on a private verbal codeword with family members to verify identities during unexpected or emergency calls.
Never pay via untraceable methods: Legitimate agencies and law enforcement will not demand payment via wire transfers, prepaid debit cards, Bitcoin, or cryptocurrency.
Do not click text or email links: Avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages regarding traffic tickets, DMV fees, or utility discounts.
Illinois Attorney General’s Scam Hotline: Call 1-800-243-0618
Local Law Enforcement / Sheriff's Office : Contact your local police non-emergency dispatch (e.g., Bloomington Police Department at 309-820-8888)
Federal Trade Commission (FTC): Report fraud online at Report Fraud FTC

text_blocks.snippet: If you suspect you or someone you know has been targeted, let me know what type of communication you received (phone call, text, or email) so I can provide specific steps on what to do next.
